title.narrative: World Bank PID Trust Fund for Palestine 2023-2026
World Bank PID Trust Fund för Palestina 2023-2026

description.narrative: The Partnership for Infrastructure Development (PID) Multi Donor Trust Fund's (MDTF) Project Development objective is to improve coverage, quality and sustainability of infrastructure in Palestine in the water, urban development and energy sectors. The design of the program is intended to support the core principles of sustainability, partnership, client-driven ownership, harmonization, and knowledge building. The PID MDTF predominantly provides co-financing to investment operations implemented by the Palestinian Authority (PA). The PID MDTF supports the PA to achieve its sectoral objectives to improving basic service delivery and performance across the water, energy and urban development sectors. Projects co-financed by the PID MDTF focus both on infrastructure financing and capacity building with the objective to improve service delivery, strengthen key institutions, and advance critical sector reforms. The Trust Fund (TF) provides financing for infrastructure projects and programs, and analytical and advisory activities that the World Bank (WB) is supporting in the water, urban development, and energy sectors. The operations in the TF are according to the WBs support for the PAs strategic long-term plans for development.

Det övergripande utvecklingsmålet för World Bank Partnership for Infrastructure Development Multi-Donor Trust Fund (PID MDTF) är att förbättra täckningen, kvaliteten och hållbarheten för infrastrukturen i Palestina (som inte är i område C) genom ekonomiskt och tekniskt bistånd till Palestinian Authority (PA) för utveckling av infrastruktur och relaterad kapacitetsuppbyggnad och institutionell utveckling inom vatten-, stadsutvecklings- och energisektorerna. Fonden stöder PA:s ansträngningar att genomföra den nationella utvecklingsplanen (NDP) 2021-2023.

The overall development objective for the World Bank Partnership for Infrastructure Development Multi-Donor Trust Fund (PID MDTF) is to improve the coverage, quality, and sustainability of infrastructure in Palestine (that is not in area C) through financial and technical assistance to the Palestinian Authority (PA) for infrastructure development and related capacity building and institutional development in the water, urban development, and energy sectors. The Trust Fund supports the PA’s efforts to implement the National Development Plan (NDP) 2021-2023.

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The Partnership for Infrastructure Development (PID) Multi-Donor Trust Fund continued to generate important institutional and service delivery results across the urban, water and energy sectors despite a challenging operating environment. While implementation in Gaza remained largely suspended because of conflict and access restrictions, the programme demonstrated significant progress in strengthening Palestinian institutions, improving service delivery in the West Bank, and maintaining readiness for future recovery. The results below are drawn from the FY26 Semi-Annual Report.
1. Strengthened land administration and property rights
The first Real Estate Registration Project (RERP) successfully achieved its development objectives by registering 169,514 land titles and reducing the average time required to register property from 10.5 months to five months. These changes improve tenure security, increase administrative efficiency and provide a stronger foundation for municipal finance and private sector investment. The Palestinian Land Authority has strengthened its capacity to provide faster, more efficient and increasingly digital property registration services, improving how land administration is carried out.
The launch of the Second Real Estate Registration Project (RERP II) ensures that these institutional improvements will continue, while introducing digital property services and modernised information systems to improve service accessibility for property owners.
2. Municipal institutions strengthened and service delivery improved
The Resilient Municipal Services Project (RMSP) is progressing well, with five of six indicators on track. Municipalities have improved their capacity to deliver accountable and resilient services while preparations for a national Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfer system represent an important step toward more predictable and transparent municipal financing.
Citizen satisfaction reached 93 percent, reflecting visible improvements in roads, lighting and public spaces. Municipalities have also expanded communication through digital platforms and successfully resolved 37 citizen complaints through strengthened grievance mechanisms.
Thus, municipal governments are increasingly using digital communication, citizen feedback and more accountable financial management practices to improve local service delivery.
3. Water sector institutions advancing despite conflict
Although major infrastructure activities in Gaza remain suspended, important institutional reforms continued in the West Bank. The Northeast Jenin Regional Water Utility was formally established, while consultations advanced for additional regional utilities. Procurement for major infrastructure under the Water Security and Resilience Programme (WSRP-1) progressed, and coordination between the Palestinian Water Authority, Water Sector Regulatory Council, National Water Company and service providers has strengthened. The National Water Company also continued its institutional transformation.
Water sector institutions are increasingly coordinating planning, regulation and service delivery through regional utility models and performance-based management approaches, strengthening sector governance.
4. Energy sector institutions improving governance and renewable energy deployment
The ASPIRE programme continued strengthening the institutional performance of the Palestinian energy sector despite severe implementation constraints. Medium-voltage network upgrades increased to 60.4 km, while beneficiaries served through distributed solar photovoltaic systems increased from 60 to 305.
Competitive procurement for 20.6 MW of utility-scale solar generation progressed, while technical assistance supported improvements in operational performance, investment readiness and regulatory capacity.
The result of this on an actors level is that the Palestinian Energy and Natural Resources Authority, the Palestinian Electricity Transmission Company and the Palestinian Electricity Regulatory Council have strengthened planning, procurement and regulatory practices, while increasingly integrating renewable energy into sector planning and implementation.
5. Advisory work influencing national policies and future investments
Analytical and advisory support generated important policy-level results. The completed Solid Waste Management Roadmap informed both the Integrated Solid Waste Management Project and the Palestinian Authority's new National Solid Waste Management Strategy (20252029). Energy sector analytical work informed the design of ASPIRE Phase III, while technical support contributed to Gaza recovery planning and the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment.
The newly approved Palestinian Investment Preparation Facility will strengthen the Ministry of Finance and Planning's capacity to prepare and manage future infrastructure investments.
6. Gender equality and inclusion outcomes exceeded targets
Several projects exceeded gender-related targets. Under RERP, 32.8 percent of registered property titles were issued in women's names, exceeding the target of 30 percent. RMSP achieved 60 percent satisfaction among female beneficiaries, surpassing its target, while ASPIRE reached its target of 19 percent female engineers employed in the energy sector ahead of schedule. WSRP also exceeded its target for female interns (15 compared with a target of 10).
7. Climate resilience and institutional preparedness strengthened
Climate resilience remains a core feature of the PID portfolio, with 68 percent climate co-benefits across active investments, substantially exceeding the World Bank target of 45 percent.
Municipalities demonstrated stronger climate planning by submitting 26 resilience project proposals, of which five were selected for implementation in areas including water, sanitation, solid waste, irrigation and stormwater management.
